method: One row per item of docs/parity/inventory-air.json, in its order (ids copied). For each item the implementing code was found by: (1) the opcode constant / builder in jhmesh/messages.py, jhmesh/vendor_models.py, jhmesh/config_messages.py; (2) its sender: grep of the builder name in custom_components/junghome_ble/*.py and tools/cli_ops.py; (3) its receiver: the STATUS_HANDLERS registry (grep '@register_status_handler' in coordinator.py and 'register_status_handler(' in config_entities.py / climate.py); an opcode with no entry is not consumed; (4) for vendor property ids: jhmesh/properties.py PropertySpec + config_entities.describe()/FIRST_PAGE/UNSAFE_PROPERTIES/cacheable() and sensor.py; (5) for non-access kinds: jhmesh/client.py (_on_network_pdu, _parse_beacon, _on_segment, _send_ack, _is_replay), jhmesh/pdu.py, jhmesh/sniffer.py. Tests: a python walk over tests/**/*.py mapping each 'def test_*' to the property ids / builder names / handler names it mentions; a test is only cited when it sends, injects or asserts the message (not merely names it). Status rules: implemented = code in the integration or tools/ CLI plus a test exercising it with the on-air encoding; partial = code without a test, or the on-air behaviour (encoding, who sends, consumption) not matched; gap = decoded at most by describe()/catalogue with no consumer or sender. Items sent on air only by the development tool (unicast-unknown) count as implemented when tools/cli_ops.py builds them. No item was judged na. STATUS RULES, made exact in the adversarial verification pass (so a rerun lands on the same status): implemented = a sender (for what HA/the CLI originates on air) or a specific consumer (for what others originate) exists in the integration or tools/, a test exercises it with the on-air encoding, and the on-air role (sender, solicited vs unsolicited) is matched; partial = such a sender/consumer exists but without a test of the on-air encoding, or the on-air behaviour is not matched; gap = no sender and no specific consumer anywhere in the integration or tools/ - library builders without a caller, describe(), the property catalogue and the generic per-message accounting of _on_message (last_heard / liveness, coordinator.py:3403) do not count; na = nothing to match (field has no behaviour for the app or HA). Verification also checked mechanically that every cited file:line exists and is non-blank and every cited test function exists; air:adv:* rows cover the items appended to the inventory from docs/bluetooth-recheck.md sec. 1. UPDATE: 56 rows added for the items of settings.json (the phone app's settings session). Rule used for them, on top of the status rules: a message HA itself sends or consumes with the same encoding is implemented (its builder, sender / consumer and a test of the encoding are cited, mostly from the msg / prop rows of the same message); a message only the app sends whose behaviour another row judges (a property HA reads through another server, a read HA does not do) is dup of that row. Citations: every `code` entry is now `path::symbol` (docs/parity/README.md, Row schema), converted from `path:line` by reading each line in the tree its ledger line was written against (git blame), following it through every later re-pointing that kept the cited text and past the merges that re-pointed lines to other code, and naming the innermost symbol holding it; `tools/parity.py check` verifies each symbol is defined.

rows.reason: Every Scene Status (0x5E) is a STATUS_HANDLERS entry: a success keeps the element's current scene (ElementState.scene; the scene entity's active_members) and, published to a group (any destination that is no unicast address: a Status sent to the app, the gateway or us answers a Scene Get and only updates the state — the blacklist proxy filter delivers all three) for a scene no recall reported within SCENE_RECALL_WINDOW (5 s; the captured statuses follow the recall within 50 ms), fires junghome_ble_scene_recalled without source, with reported_by, and records the scene entity's activation. A recall is noted where its scene event fires; the hub publishes a key's recall whether or not the key's event entity is enabled (review-4 H4-2), so the members' Status reports only a recall nobody else told of. The connect-time refresh reads each CTL light's temperature element (el1) with 0x8261 right after its range Get on el0, as the gateway reads a tunable-white light (settings capture: 0x8262 to the lights' el0 0210 / 016A, 0x8261 to their el1 016B / 026F / 0233); the 0x8266 answer lands on the light through _on_ctl_temperature_status. No extra Get after another client's 0x8264: the gateway polls el1 with 0x8261 all day (1521 Gets in the captures, against 79 gateway 0x8264), and the 0x8266 answers it gets are forwarded to HA by the proxy's empty blacklist filter and applied whatever their destination, so a Get of ours would only add to that traffic. Its silence does not count toward the node's reachability (_get_state counted=False): it is the third Get to the same node in one refresh, after the light's own state and range, and one the app never sends; under the app's rule one unanswered request marks the node at once (_missed_answer), and the light's own state Get already decides that.

rows.missing: PB-ADV PDUs are captured and labelled but not decoded: no parsing of the Generic Provisioning PDU (Link Open with the device UUID, Link Ack/Close, Transaction Start/Continuation/Ack), so the sniffer cannot say which device is being provisioned or whether a provisioning of this installation (app adding a node) started/failed. Build: a PB-ADV / Generic Provisioning PDU decoder in jhmesh/sniffer.py (spec layouts, tested with synthetic PDUs and the captured PB-ADV records). Provisioning over PB-ADV itself is not possible from HA (no raw advertising TX through HA Bluetooth).
